holly-bush.notes: Grade II, Fuller's since 2010, multi-room interior with a real fire, seasonal menu, listed among Fuller's best Sunday roasts.

spaniards-inn.notes: 1500s inn, canopy-sheltered terrace and big garden by the Heath, dog friendly, praised Sunday roast.

flask-highgate.notes: Grade II Fuller's pub, since at least 1663. Large front yard partly covered and heated; two real fires; five beers on tap.

wenlock-arms.notes: 1835 corner pub, ten handpumps of cask and real cider, CAMRA North London Pub of the Year 2026 and 2017. Snacks only.

compton-arms.notes: Kitchen residency Rake (Wed to Sun) after Four Legs, Belly and Tiella; Top 50 Gastropubs listed. Back snug and garden. Orwell's model pub.

patch.food.note: Chef residency Rake cooks Wednesday to Sunday; eat in the snug, the garden or the bar

drapers-arms.notes: 44 Barnsbury St. Garden and private dining room, famous Sunday roast, Top 50 Gastropubs. Book ahead.

bull-and-last.notes: 168 Highgate Rd, coaching inn from 1721 rebuilt 1883, six bedrooms, modern British menu, Top 50 Gastropubs.

edinboro-castle.notes: Grade II 1839 pub on Mornington Terrace. Garden seats 300 with heated fairy-lit canopies and large screens for live sport; dog friendly.

grafton.notes: 20 Prince of Wales Rd. British Pub of the Year 2015. Sky Sports on multiple screens and projectors in all areas. Home to Texas Joe's BBQ plus Sunday roast. All-weather heated roof terrace with retractable awnings. Live music, child and dog friendly.

patch.food.note: Texas Joe's BBQ in residence plus flat iron steaks and a full Sunday roast

old-dairy.notes: 1-3 Crouch Hill, listed Victorian dairy with exterior friezes. Six screens with all Sky and TNT channels, popular with Arsenal fans, above-average food.

gunners.notes: 204 Blackstock Rd, noon to midnight daily. Packed with Arsenal memorabilia, shows every live TV match with Arsenal taking preference, live music venue inside, dog friendly.

arsenal-tavern.notes: Renamed Brook Gate after a 2023 refurbishment by new owners, but still a go-to Gunners match-day pub: two pool tables, match-day drinks offers, more screens than you can count.

patch.name: Brook Gate (ex Arsenal Tavern)
patch.tip: The old Arsenal Tavern, renamed Brook Gate in 2023 but still red and white on match days. Roomy, two pool tables, screens everywhere.

auld-triangle.notes: The Auld Triangle closed in 2021 and reopened as The Plimsoll, a food-led pub from the Four Legs team famous for its cheeseburger. Still popular with Arsenal fans pre-match, no longer an Irish sports pub.

patch.name: The Plimsoll

food.note: Four Legs' kitchen: one of London's best cheeseburgers and a short, sharp menu

patch.tip: The old Auld Triangle, now The Plimsoll: a Victorian corner pub with one of London's best cheeseburgers. Arsenal fans still pass through, but nobody's shouting at a screen.

woodbine.notes: 215 Blackstock Rd, independent Irish bar since 1919, Arsenal supporter for a century. Thai food Mon-Fri, pub food and roasts at weekends. Walk-in only, no bookings.

food.note: Thai kitchen on weekdays, pub food and roasts at the weekend

patch.tip: Independent Irish pub on Blackstock Road, Arsenal through and through since 1919. Thai in the week, roasts at the weekend, no bookings.

highbury-barn.notes: The Highbury Barn Tavern, reopened after a 500k refurbishment in 2025 with a new chef. Shows all Arsenal games; match-day BBQ on the canopied terrace with Godfrey's sausages; roasts 12 to 9 on Sundays. 11 min walk to the Emirates.

patch.name: The Highbury Barn Tavern
patch.food.note: Match-day BBQ on the terrace, big-screen Saturdays with a match-day menu, roasts 12 to 9 on Sundays

lamb-holloway.notes: 54 Holloway Rd. Three rotating cask ales and 12 keg lines, mostly London breweries. Irish session Tuesdays, folk Sundays, bluegrass monthly. CAMRA North London POTY finalist 2025.

salisbury-harringay.notes: Grade II* 1899 gin palace on CAMRA's national inventory. Function room with a 120-inch screen for major sporting events; cheap and good roast; jukebox; hotel rooms.

great-northern-railway-tavern.notes: 1897, Grade II, CAMRA two-star national inventory interior. Hornsey's biggest pub garden on two tiers with bookable areas and an outdoor kebab shop Thursday to Saturday.

patch.food.note: Fuller's kitchen, Sunday roast, and an outdoor kebab shop in the garden Thursday to Saturday

bluecoats.notes: 1835 former school on the High Road. Beer garden screened by plants, a huge pull-down screen in the rear corner for football, resident kitchen, function room, 2am licence on match days.

corner-pin.notes: 732 High Rd, restored by the club and reopened in 2021 with Beavertown, relaunched Aug 2024 run by Spurs. Three floors, rear garden. Closed to the public on Spurs match days.

patch.tip: Restored by the club opposite the stadium, three floors and a garden. Note: closed to the public on match days, so it's a non-match-day Spurs pilgrimage.

bell-walthamstow.notes: 617 Forest Rd, Social Pub and Kitchen group. Grand corner pub with an open fire, sofas, a massive beer garden and live sport. Sunday roast with a nut roast option, kids eat free with roasts.

nags-head-walthamstow.notes: 1857 village pub, motto Pizza, Ale, Cats. Four handpumps, Italian food and pizza, heated walled garden with fairy lights, live jazz, resident cats. Children in the garden only until 7.30.

food.note: Pizza and Italian plates, eaten in the bar or the walled garden

chequers-walthamstow.notes: 145 High St, on the site since 1699. Rotating local beers (Five Points, Pillars, Wild Card), enormous courtyard garden with games, pub classics kitchen, all live sport on multiple big screens with Sky, TNT and Amazon.

food.note: Pub classics and something a bit different from the kitchen

rose-and-crown-walthamstow.notes: 53 Hoe St. Theatre upstairs, proper pub downstairs; home of the Red Imp Comedy Club and Walthamstow Folk Club; up to six ale pumps with microbrewery guests; rotating food menus. CAMRA East London POTY finalist.

food.note: Rotating kitchen residencies

clissold-arms.notes: 105 Fortis Green. Site of the Kinks' first gig; Kinks Room full of memorabilia. Five areas: restaurant, Kinks Room, covered terrace, shed and garden. Home-made Greek and traditional dishes, family-orientated, private hire.

patch.food.note: Home-made Greek dishes alongside pub classics and a Sunday roast, in the restaurant, terrace or garden

auld-shillelagh.notes: Long narrow Irish bar, routinely named for the best Guinness in London. TV screens throughout with big-screen football and racing, framed shirts, live music.

jolly-butchers.notes: 204 Stoke Newington High St. Seven real ales, three ciders, big bottle list, contemporary North Indian food from Booma Kitchen. Guardian top-10 UK pub. Cask bar since 2010.

food.note: Booma Kitchen's North Indian menu, eaten in the big high-ceilinged bar

three-crowns-stokey.notes: Corner of Church St and the High St. Relaunched as Stokey's football pub: every televised Premier League fixture live on three new screens with sound; The Waiting Room basement with DJs and match screenings; award-winning food, live jazz, late nights. Bookable football tables on OpenTable.

rose-and-crown-stokey.notes: 199 Church St, Grade II 1930-32 Truman's house on CAMRA's regional inventory, log fires, bay windows, seven en-suite rooms. Quiz Tuesday 8pm. Pub classics, burgers, roast.

shakespeare-stokey.notes: 57 Allen Rd, 1850, the oldest pub building in Stoke Newington, Remarkable Pubs. London Pride and two rotating beers, no kitchen but bring pizza in from next door.

patch.food.note: No kitchen; bring a pizza in from the shop next door

old-red-lion.notes: 418 St John St, on the site since 1415, 60-seat fringe theatre upstairs. Shows a lot of Premier League including 3pm Saturday games; long-time HQ of the Capital Canaries (Norwich City supporters). Five real ales, Neapolitan pizzas.

food.note: Hand-made Neapolitan pizzas

hemingford-arms.notes: 1855 Barnsbury local with a floral exterior, Thai kitchen, quiz Wednesdays, live music, good Guinness, function room upstairs.

albion-barnsbury.notes: 10 Thornhill Rd. Georgian pub with a 450 sq m wisteria-covered garden, one of Islington's finest. Kitchen praised by the Guardian, Observer and Independent; Sunday roasts of pork belly, Texel lamb and aged topside.

parcel-yard.notes: Grade I listed, two floors next to platform 9 at King's Cross. 12 large screens with room for 200+ fans, Premier League, Champions League and Six Nations; bookings taken for football. 40+ draught lines, seasonal menu.

lighterman.notes: Three floors on Granary Square and Regent's Canal with terraces on every level and a wraparound top-floor terrace. Modern British menu, weekend brunch, Sunday roast and DJ sets from 4pm on Sundays.

queens-head-kx.notes: 66 Acton St, Mother Kelly's family. Victorian interior with listed tiles and fireplace; up to three real ciders (CAMRA London Cider Pub of the Year 2013 and 2016); piano Thursdays and Sundays, monthly jazz, comedy, folk and quiz nights.

big-chill-house.notes: 257-259 Pentonville Rd. Open until midnight most nights and 3am Fri-Sat, hot food 12-10, DJs until the early hours at weekends, roof terrace available for hire.

oxford-kentish-town.notes: The Oxford Tavern at 256 Kentish Town Rd has become The Parakeet, a Top 50 Gastropub with an open kitchen; craft beers, function room, live and electronic music nights, kitchen takeovers. No live sport offer found.

patch.name: The Parakeet (ex Oxford Tavern)

food.note: Top 50 Gastropub cooking from the open kitchen, roast on Sundays

patch.tip: The old Oxford Tavern reborn as The Parakeet: a Top 50 gastropub with an open kitchen and a Victorian shell. Concert-goers from the Forum before, diners after.

worlds-end-camden.notes: 174 Camden High St, sprawling Victorian corner site with two bars, mezzanine and the 500-capacity Underworld venue below. Big TV screens for live sport.

blues-kitchen-camden.notes: 111-113 Camden High St. Live music every night from about 9.30pm, DJs until the small hours, open until 2.30am Fri and 3am Sat. In-house BBQ smoked over fruit woods: brisket, ribs, burnt ends.

wells-hampstead.notes: The Wells Tavern, 30 Well Walk, Grade II c.1849. Award-winning gastropub since 2003 with elegant upstairs dining rooms and a ground-floor bar.

freemasons-arms.notes: Large garden by the Heath, first recorded 1820. Basement holds London's only surviving old English skittle alley; the pell mell court was dug up in the 1990s. Dining pub, new cocktail menu.

patch.tip: Huge garden right by the Heath and the last London skittles alley in the capital, down in the basement.

garden-gate.notes: 14 South End Rd, a minute from Hampstead Heath station. Spacious garden with heaters and summer BBQ, cask ales, home-cooked pub grub. Open until midnight Fri and Sat.

washington-belsize.notes: 50 England's Lane, Grade II c.1865 with spectacular back-painted mirrors and glazed screening. Known for Victorian character and dining rather than sport; no screens offer found.

patch.tip: Grade II Victorian pub on England's Lane with back-painted mirrors and a proper dining room. Not a sports pub.

sir-richard-steele.notes: 97 Haverstock Hill, independent, opens 4pm, asset of community value. Regular comedy, music and quiz nights in the upper bar.

black-lion-kilburn.notes: 274 Kilburn High Rd, Grade II* with gilded Adam-style plasterwork, CAMRA conservation award, boutique hotel rooms. Listed as showing no live TV sport.

patch.tip: Grade II* gin palace with an extraordinary gilded ceiling and hotel rooms upstairs. Dining and drinking, not screens.

north-london-tavern.notes: 375 Kilburn High Rd, 1894 Victorian pub with original features, Greene King. Gastro restaurant room at the rear, ambitious evening menu, quiz and live music, dog friendly.

torch-wembley.notes: 1-5 Bridge Rd, built 1956, refurbished 2019, Greene King Flaming Grill. Sky and TNT on two big screens plus others, outside bar on match days, two pool tables, big car park.

food.note: Flaming Grill menu of burgers, ribs and mixed grills

green-man-wembley.notes: Dagmar Ave, pub and hotel ten minutes from the stadium. Expansive beer garden with a children's playground, outdoor beer sellers and a BBQ on match days; Englandfans members get 50p off a pint.

canonbury-tavern.notes: Canonbury Place, pub since the early 1700s, rebuilt 1846. Very large partially covered garden to the side and rear (closes 9pm), British seasonal food, real ales, traditional Irish music sessions, very dog friendly.

alwyne-castle.notes: 83 St Paul's Rd. Sky TV showing major events on a big screen; garden holds 300 with an outside bar and heaters, plus a conservatory and courtyard.

marquess-tavern.notes: 32 Canonbury St, Grade II c.1854 with double-height ceilings, real fire, street patio; now a Punch pub. London Pride and Landlord among three cask ales.

old-queens-head.notes: 44 Essex Rd, 1830s corner building. House and disco DJs Fridays, RnB and hip-hop Saturdays, karaoke room, pub quiz. Open until 2am Fri and Sat.

castle-islington.notes: 54 Pentonville Rd. Partially covered roof terrace with views across Islington and one big screen for sport, three TVs inside. British food, Sunday roasts, bottomless brunch, dog friendly.

narrowboat.notes: 119 St Peter's St, Young's since 2012, the only pub directly on Regent's Canal in Islington. Two canal-side balconies, three handpumps, famous Bloody Marys, seasonal menu and Sunday roasts.

hope-and-anchor.notes: 207 Upper St, 1880, Grade II, Greene King. Pub-rock and punk heritage (Stranglers live album), still regular live music, Hope Theatre upstairs, rock jukebox.

lexington.notes: 96-98 Pentonville Rd. 250-capacity venue upstairs, bourbon bar below. Rough Trade pop quiz Mondays, DJs. Open until 2am most nights, 3am Thursday, 4am Friday and Saturday.

camden-head-islington.notes: Camden Passage, 1899 Grade II with etched glass and a circular bar, Greene King. Free Angel Comedy Club upstairs every night. Pies and fish and chips, large beer garden, fireplace.

food.note: Hearty pies and fish and chips

dove-broadway-market.notes: 24-28 Broadway Market, family-run for 30+ years. Over 100 bottled Belgian and world beers plus six guest ales. Belgian and British food, famous sausages and burgers, Thai menu Tuesdays, beer-dough pizzas, live music in the evenings, booths and snugs.

cat-and-mutton.notes: 76 Broadway Market, pub since 1729. Two air-conditioned floors equipped for major football and rugby fixtures; funk, soul and disco DJs Fri to Sun from 9pm; quiz Tuesdays; famous Sunday roasts; Hackney's biggest private room for hire.

chesham-arms.notes: Traditional Homerton boozer saved by its community, with a garden and fireplaces; child and dog friendly.

adam-and-eve-homerton.notes: 155 Homerton High St, mid-18th century. Victorian walled garden with a quirky covered section, L-shaped pool table and darts, sports and DJs, food from 4pm weekdays. Open until 1am Fri and Sat.

pembury-tavern.notes: 90 Amhurst Rd, Five Points Brewing's pub since 2018. Two guest ales and 16 keg lines, ACE Pizza in the kitchen, bar billiards, screens for big matches kept at a civilised volume, quiz Mondays, monthly comedy. CAMRA community pub of the year 2020.

scolt-head.notes: De Beauvoir local with a large projector room for football and rugby plus smaller screens in the bar. Tree-lined front garden, summer BBQs, pool, live music, quiz.

shacklewell-arms.notes: 71 Shacklewell Lane. Gig room, pub space, smoking area; gigs all week and DJ nights at weekends. Open 5pm to midnight Mon-Thu, 5pm to 3am Fri-Sat, 3-11 Sun.

victoria-dalston.notes: 451 Queensbridge Rd, JaguarShoes Collective. 200-capacity venue with a full sound system, decades on the East London DIY gig circuit. Quiz not confirmed.

duke-of-wellington-dalston.notes: 119 Balls Pond Rd, 1820s pub with historic fittings and a mosaic floor; site of London's first pub theatre in 1967. CAMRA real-ale award, ideal for a football match, outdoor seating.

prince-george-dalston.notes: 40 Parkholme Rd. Quiz Monday 7pm, comedy nights, life drawing, full food menu, garden, live sports screenings. Open until 1am Fri and Sat.

food.note: Full pub menu

crate-brewery.notes: Former print factory on the River Lea, brewery and pizzeria since 2012. Stone-baked pizzas, upcycled interior, canalside tables. Noon to 11pm weekdays, midnight weekends, DJs Fri and Sat.

howling-hops.notes: Queens Yard, the UK's first tank bar: ten beers straight from the tanks along a ten-metre bar, beer-hall space and garden. La Cumbia Latin kitchen, live music Fridays, vinyl DJs Saturdays.

food.note: La Cumbia's tacos, burritos and loaded fries

star-hackney-downs.notes: Corner of Queensdown Rd on the edge of the park. Huge garden with outdoor TVs, big screen and TNT; covered heated terrace; pizzas, burgers and cocktails; regularly screens tournaments outside.

food.note: Pizzas and burgers, eaten in the garden

clapton-hart.notes: Antic pub on a site licensed since 1722. Big beer garden with a massive outdoor screen for major events, first come first served. Eight mostly local draught ales; kitchen led by an ex-Ottolenghi chef.

patch.food.note: Kitchen led by an ex-Ottolenghi chef, plus Sunday roast

crooked-billet-clapton.notes: 84 Upper Clapton Rd, on the site since 1731, Young's. One of East London's biggest gardens with covered cabins, sunny all day and heated at night, decked over the old car park. Roasts, pub classics, pizzas and burgers; DJ nights, weekly quiz, monthly movie nights.

food.note: Pizzas, burgers, pub classics and a Sunday roast, mostly eaten in the garden

anchor-and-hope-clapton.notes: 15 High Hill Ferry, c.1850, one of Fuller's smallest pubs on the bank of the Lea. One panelled bar, dartboard, wood fire, ESB and Pride. No kitchen but a Jamaican food truck nearby delivers to the pub.

patch.food.note: No kitchen; the Jamaican food truck along the towpath delivers to your table

princess-of-wales-clapton.notes: 146 Lea Bridge Rd, Young's (Geronimo). Large multi-area bar with a stove, covered and heated riverside garden on the Lea Valley Walk, screens for the Six Nations and Wimbledon.

marksman.notes: 254 Hackney Rd. First London pub named Michelin Pub of the Year; owners ex-St John. Wood-panelled bar, first-floor dining room, rooftop terrace, one of London's best Sunday roasts, 50+ wines, local beers.

camel-bethnal-green.notes: 277 Globe Rd, Victorian pub saved from demolition by locals. Award-winning home-made pies and mash, Sambrook's Wandle plus two changing ales, south-facing garden.

approach-tavern.notes: 47 Approach Rd, 1860s, rebuilt after wartime bomb damage. 20 beers on tap, hearty food, beer garden, dog friendly, internationally known Approach Gallery upstairs.

sun-tavern.notes: 441 Bethnal Green Rd. Cocktails, 40+ Irish whiskeys, poitin and local craft beer. Noon to midnight Sun-Wed, 2am Thu-Sat, live music at weekends and DJs late.

carpenters-arms-cheshire.notes: 73 Cheshire St, Victorian freehouse bought by the Krays for their mother in 1967. More than 30 beers on keg and in bottle, refurbished but with its history intact.

sebright-arms.notes: 31-35 Coate St off Hackney Rd. Basement venue with gigs almost nightly, many free; early shows for Charli XCX and Squid. Slap and Pickle burgers in residence, 1930s East End interior.

patch.food.note: Slap and Pickle's burgers from the resident kitchen

star-of-bethnal-green.notes: 359 Bethnal Green Rd, Electric Star. DJs and karaoke Thursday to Sunday, five private karaoke booths upstairs (Karaoke Heaven), drag brunch, quiz, live sports screenings, open until 2am Fri and Sat.

ten-bells.notes: 84 Commercial St, the Jack the Ripper pub with Victorian tiles. Open until midnight Sun-Wed and 1am Thu-Sat.

pride-of-spitalfields.notes: 3 Heneage St, small free house off Brick Lane, decades in the Good Beer Guide, always busy. Lenny the cat, a piano for customers, bring-your-own-records Mondays.

golden-heart.notes: 110 Commercial St, Grade II 1936 Truman's pub. Sandra Esquilant has run it since 1978; Britart local for Emin, Lucas and Gilbert and George, with Emin pieces on the walls.

owl-and-pussycat.notes: 34 Redchurch St, Grade II 18th-century building (originally The Crown), Brakspear. Sunny rear garden with cover and heaters, leather sofas by a roaring fire, seasonal British pub grub, The Jago cocktail bar upstairs for bookings.

well-and-bucket.notes: 143 Bethnal Green Rd, tiled Victorian gin palace from 1850 restored by Urban Pubs and Bars. Oysters and sliders, 75-bottle beer list, cask that sells out, small garden, 5CC candlelit cocktail bar in the basement.

crown-and-shuttle.notes: 226 Shoreditch High St, 1865 pub reopened 2013 after years boarded up. One of East London's largest beer gardens with a tarp roof and food truck; craft beers, cocktails, burgers and plenty of vegan dishes.

old-fountain.notes: 3 Baldwin St, freehouse run by the Durrant family since 1964. Eight real ales and five craft kegs downstairs, heated roof terrace with parasols upstairs, CAMRA beer award 2013.

grapes-limehouse.notes: 76 Narrow St, Grade II 1720s building on a 1583 pub site, part-owned by Ian McKellen, Sean Mathias and Evgeny Lebedev. Veranda over the Thames, Dickens connection, fish upstairs.

narrow-limehouse.notes: Gordon Ramsay's The Narrow at 44 Narrow St has been rebranded Bread Street Kitchen and Bar Limehouse. Large riverside terrace with a summer BBQ and panoramic Thames views; more restaurant than pub now.

patch.name: Bread Street Kitchen & Bar (ex The Narrow)
patch.tip: Gordon Ramsay's riverside spot on the bend at Limehouse, now trading as Bread Street Kitchen. The terrace and the view are the point.

prospect-of-whitby.notes: Built 1520, the country's oldest riverside tavern, Greene King. Beer garden, first-floor balcony and a rooftop terrace with river views; cask ales, fish and chips, Sunday roast. Pepys, Dickens, Turner and a hanging noose outside.

town-of-ramsgate.notes: 62 Wapping High St, Grade II, present building 1758 with a 1937 interior. Long narrow bar, riverside beer garden by Wapping Old Stairs, three regular ales plus a guest, home-cooked food all day, children and dogs welcome.

captain-kidd.notes: 108 Wapping High St, Sam Smith's in a Grade II former coffee warehouse converted in the 1980s. Three floors, nautical theme, cobbled riverside terrace almost touching the water at high tide. One cask ale (Old Brewery Bitter).

cow-westfield.notes: Chestnut Plaza, Westfield Stratford, overlooking the London Stadium. Big screens for Premier League, Champions League and tournaments; packed with Hammers before every home game; pub classics, steaks, cask ales.

king-edward-vii.notes: 47 Broadway, Grade II early-18th-century pub (once the King of Prussia), tiled walls, frosted glass dividers, sunken bar, back room and small patio. Closed late 2025 and reopened after a major renovation in September 2026.

patch.tip: The King Eddie: Stratford's Georgian survivor with tiled walls and a panelled back room, freshly reopened in September 2026 after a full renovation.

red-lion-leytonstone.notes: 640 High Rd, 1870s, bought from Antic by Urban Pubs and Bars in September 2024. Enormous garden revamped with heated booths, a covered area and screens including a massive screen for big events; upstairs ballroom where Led Zeppelin reputedly played their first gig.

patch.food.note: Urban Pubs and Bars kitchen, pub classics and roast
patch.tip: Leytonstone's grand old pub with a huge garden of heated booths and a giant screen, and a ballroom upstairs with Led Zeppelin history.

heathcote-and-star.notes: 344 Grove Green Rd. Leytonstone's largest garden, two function rooms, screens throughout the pub for football and boxing. Award-winning Dragon Flame BBQ kitchen plus Krapow Thai street food in the garden.

food.note: Dragon Flame's British BBQ inside and Krapow's Thai street food in the garden

northcote-arms.notes: 110 Grove Green Rd, historic interior with five separate areas and two large gardens. Sports TV for big games, extra ales on Orient home days, pub games, live music, drag, music bingo, vinyl and folk nights; dog and family friendly.

leyton-technical.notes: Grade II former Leyton Town Hall (1896 technical college), pop-up in 2012, closed 2022 and reopened September 2024 as an upscale gastrobar with up to eight real ales and ciders. Home fans only on Orient match days. CAMRA lists it as Leyton Engineer.

food.note: Gastrobar menu in the old council chambers

patch.tip: In the old Leyton Town Hall, minutes from Brisbane Road, reopened in 2024 with eight real ales. Home fans only on match days.

leyton-star.notes: 116 High Rd, Electric Star group. Garden of covered wooden booths with heaters and a private TV in every booth plus a main garden screen; long tables for big groups.

birkbeck-tavern.notes: 45 Langthorne Rd, 1881, saved from developers in 2012. Walled garden, pool table, two dartboards. The designated away pub for Leyton Orient, popular with home and away fans on match days.

patch.tip: Leyton's proper backstreet local with a walled garden and real ale. Orient's designated away pub, so both sets of fans before kick-off.

forest-tavern.notes: Forest Lane, outside Forest Gate station, c.1870. Antic from 2013, Portobello Pubs since late 2020. Six changing ale pumps, food and Sunday roasts, rear garden, quiz, DJs, vinyl fairs, open mic, live music.

coborn.notes: 8 Coborn Rd, Young's. Seasonal British menu and a famous Aberdeen Angus roast with double-egg Yorkshires; cult Sunday quiz at 7.30 that books out.

morgan-arms.notes: 43 Morgan St, rebuilt 1891-2, carved wooden bar and stained glass. Seasonal British gastropub menu, recommended Sunday roast, craft beer and cocktails, dogs and families welcome.

lord-tredegar.notes: 50 Lichfield Rd, Grade II mid-19th century, Remarkable Pubs since 2012. Traditional bar, back dining room with an open kitchen under a skylight, covered medium-sized garden by the railway, three real ales, jukebox.

palm-tree.notes: 127 Grove Rd in Mile End Park, Grade II 1935 Truman's pub with an intact interior, same family for 40+ years. Cash only, mechanical till, no telly, live jazz Thursday to Sunday often running late, two handpumps.

henry-addington.notes: Mackenzie Walk, Nicholson's. Sky and TNT on the TVs, riverside terrace with views of the towers, cask ales and traditional pub food. Three minutes from Canary Wharf station.

gun-docklands.notes: 27 Coldharbour, Grade II, 250 years old, Fuller's. Restaurant, three private dining rooms, all-weather riverside terrace for 150 facing the O2, Gin Garden; modern British food-led.

george-isle-of-dogs.notes: 114 Glengall Grove, trading as George Poplar. 1930s building with three bars, a conservatory restaurant and an award-winning vine-covered garden with big screens; Sky and TNT for Premier League and Champions League. Historic HQ of Millwall Rovers in 1889-90.

food.note: Pub kitchen and roast in the conservatory

ferry-house.notes: Pub on the site since 1722, the Island's oldest, built 1822 as the ferryman's house by the Greenwich foot tunnel. Screen and team details not confirmed.

cutty-sark-greenwich.notes: 4-6 Ballast Quay, Grade II Georgian pub over three levels, Young's. Riverside outdoor seating facing Canary Wharf and the O2, seasonal fish-led menu, three regular ales plus a guest, quiz Wednesdays.

trafalgar-tavern.notes: Park Row, Grade II, on the site since 1837 next to the Old Royal Naval College. Famous Victorian whitebait dinners; balconies and extensive riverside outdoor seating; whitebait still a speciality, roasts.

gipsy-moth.notes: 60 Greenwich Church St. Live football on indoor and outdoor screens; garden for 150 with views of the Cutty Sark, refurbished February 2026 with heated umbrellas for year-round use.

plume-of-feathers.notes: Established 1691, Greenwich's oldest pub, original fireplace and maritime relics. Award-winning garden for 50, 30-seat restaurant at the back, voted best pub in SE10 by the Greenwich Society.

greenwich-union.notes: Closed 2020, permanently 2021; absorbed into the Richard I next door. Removed.

pelton-arms.notes: Pulling pints since 1844, three original open fires, ten handpumps. Free live music several nights a week, monthly music quiz, Sky and TNT sport, bar billiards and darts.

richard-i.notes: 52-54 Royal Hill, Grade II early-17th-century buildings, Young's. Long bar into a conservatory and heated garden; extended into the former Greenwich Union next door in 2022. Nicknamed Tolly's.

white-swan-charlton.notes: Closed since March 2020; a community campaign is fundraising to buy it. Removed until it reopens.

antigallican.notes: Closed March 2018 and converted to studios; a 2023 licence application has not produced a pub. Removed.

dial-arch.notes: Royal Arsenal, 1720 gatehouse, Young's, claimed birthplace of Arsenal FC (Dial Square, 1886). Four handpumps, front beer yard for hundreds, live sport including England tournament matches.

patch.tip: Young's pub in the 1720 Royal Arsenal gatehouse where Arsenal FC was born as Dial Square. Huge courtyard, England games on the screens.

hare-and-billet.notes: 400-year-old former coaching inn overlooking the heath and its pond. Ten handpumps, Good Beer Guide 2026, famed Sunday roast, dog friendly.

princess-of-wales-blackheath.notes: 1865 bar back, long tied to Blackheath Rugby Club (changing room for the first England v Wales). Drinkers spill onto the heath in plastics; walled garden with a BBQ area; booths for groups; sought-after roasts. Screen count not confirmed.

zerodegrees-blackheath.notes: South East London's original brew-pub, opened 2000: working microbrewery, wood-fired pizzeria, mezzanine over the tanks, Bohemian room for hire. Sports screening not confirmed.

dog-and-bell.notes: 116 Prince St, independent Irish-run pub with 15 handpumps, covered beer garden, excellent food, folk nights, quizzes and an annual Pickle Festival. CAMRA Lewisham Pub of the Year 2023, 2024 and 2025.

food.note: Well-regarded pub kitchen, plus the annual Pickle Festival

royal-albert-new-cross.notes: 460 New Cross Rd, Grade II Victorian pub, ex-Antic now Portobello Brewery, refurbished and extended 2022. Up to four cask ales, Portobello house beers, burgers, raised front patio, Sunday jazz. New Cross Scene venue in the 2000s.

food.note: Burgers and pub classics, roast on Sundays

amersham-arms.notes: 388 New Cross Rd. 300-capacity back room for bands and DJs, secret gigs, cabaret, comedy (Happy Mondays club), film and theatre; live TV sport. Open until midnight Sun-Wed and 3am Thu-Sat.

job-centre-deptford.notes: Antic pub opened 2014 in the old Deptford job centre opposite the station; now trading as Jam Circus. Good cask range for Antic, rotating street-food 'kitchen hijack'.

patch.name: Jam Circus (ex Job Centre)

food.note: Rotating street-food kitchen takeovers

patch.tip: Antic's pub in the old Deptford job centre, now called Jam Circus. Late, loud, local, with a good cask list.

camberwell-arms.notes: 65 Camberwell Church St, since 2014, run by the Frank's Cafe team with chef Mike Davies. Top 50 Gastropubs 2025; sharing-only roasts from about 48 pounds for two.

hermits-cave.notes: 28 Camberwell Church St, 1902 curved-front corner pub, family-run for 25 years. Four changing beers, no music, dog friendly.

stormbird.notes: 25 Camberwell Church St, sister pub to the Hermits Cave. Six handpumps, a dozen-plus craft keg lines and nearly 100 bottles; no kitchen, bring food in.

patch.food.note: No kitchen; bring food in from the neighbours

sun-of-camberwell.notes: Coldharbour Lane, Urban Pubs and Bars, reopened June 2025 after a 1m refurbishment. Two gardens front and rear (one of Camberwell's biggest), restaurant, six handpumps, quiz Wednesdays, live music Thursdays, DJs Fridays, chess social. Sport screening not confirmed.

montpelier-peckham.notes: 43 Choumert Rd. Independent pub with a back-room cinema that screens football for major tournaments, weekly quiz, DJs Friday and Saturday, gastro food, outdoor seating, dog friendly.

prince-of-peckham.notes: Traditional pub downstairs, top-floor party room with DJs until 2.30am at weekends; big games on the big screens; kitchen by White Men Can't Jerk.

ivy-house.notes: Grade II 1930s Truman's pub, London's first co-operatively owned pub (2013), the 1970s pub-rock Newlands Tavern. Four handpumps, quiz Wednesdays, comedy and theatre Thursdays, live music Fridays, festivals.

old-nuns-head.notes: 15 Nunhead Green, 1930s mock-Tudor pub voted Time Out's best pub in London 2025. Street-food kitchen with house chefs and guest residencies (Burger Bear, Soul Cocina), Sunday roast, front and rear seating, comedy, cabaret, quiz Thursdays.

food.note: Rotating street-food kitchen with Burger Bear and Soul Cocina residencies, plus a Sunday roast

patch.tip: Time Out's best pub in London 2025: a mock-Tudor community pub on Nunhead Green with rotating kitchens, cabaret and a quiz.

gowlett.notes: 62 Gowlett Rd, corner pub with five handpumps, famed thin-crust pizzas, Lucky 7s bring-your-own-vinyl Thursdays, dogs welcome.

skehans.notes: Family-run Irish free house with multiple indoor screens and outdoor TVs in a multi-level tiered garden. Chai's Garden Thai restaurant in the old stable block, live music six nights a week, award-winning Guinness.

patch.food.note: Chai's Garden, an authentic Thai restaurant in the stable block off the garden

market-porter.notes: Stoney St, classic Victorian market pub with 12 handpumps, open 6-9am Mon-Fri for market workers, restaurant upstairs, card only.

george-inn.notes: 73-75 Borough High St, London's last galleried coaching inn, National Trust owned since 1937 and leased to Greene King. Maze of small rooms, courtyard garden, hearty dishes and Sunday roasts, Dickens connection.

rake.notes: 14 Winchester Walk, London's first craft beer bar (2006) from the Utobeer founders. At least five draught, three cask and a fridge of bottles; tiny inside with a covered terrace; wall of brewers' signatures.

anchor-bankside.notes: Historic Greene King riverside pub with a huge terrace facing St Paul's. Sources conflict on live sport: the pub's own events page advertises big-screen sport, one review says none. Treat screens as occasional.

founders-arms.notes: Glass-fronted late-1970s Young's pub on the river by Tate Modern with a large terrace, blankets and heaters year round, two regular Young's beers plus a guest, praised Sunday roasts, coffee from 9am.

angel-rotherhithe.notes: 101 Bermondsey Wall East, Grade II 1830s building on a 15th-century inn site, Sam Smith's restored Victorian interior (2005) on CAMRA's register. Dining room upstairs with Thames views and a narrow balcony; Turner painted the Fighting Temeraire from here.

woolpack-bermondsey.notes: 98 Bermondsey St. Ivy-covered rear garden with huts, covered and heated year round, summer pop-up bar; live screenings of major sport; British classics; function room; award-winning dog friendliness.

garrison.notes: 99-101 Bermondsey St, since 2003. Seasonal British gastropub with head chef Natalie Coleman (MasterChef 2013 winner) from 2025; Cinema Room downstairs for private hire up to 35.

simon-the-tanner.notes: 231 Long Lane, Grade II 1820s mid-terrace pub, ex Shepherd Neame now a free house. Three changing cask ales from small breweries plus a cider.

ancient-foresters.notes: 282 Southwark Park Rd, distinctive 1930s pub ten minutes from The Den. Stage for karaoke and live music, darts, pool, family friendly, very busy on Millwall home days.

effra-hall-tavern.notes: 38A Kellett Rd, Victorian pub with an Afro-Caribbean community feel. West Indian kitchen (jerk chicken, jollof mac and cheese), free live jazz and reggae three nights a week. Open until midnight Fri and Sat.

crown-and-anchor-brixton.notes: 246 Brixton Rd, opened 2012, Time Out's best new beer bar that year. Up to 25 taps of cask, cider and craft, big covered outdoor space, pub classics and tacos, Sunday roasts, Booma North Indian kitchen. Open until 1am Fri and Sat.

food.note: Booma's North Indian dishes alongside tacos and a Sunday roast

trinity-arms.notes: 45 Trinity Gardens, Young's, refurbished 2016, card only. Leafy garden with a large fire pit and heaters, upstairs dining room, famous roasts, dog friendly, private hire; sport shown on a low-key basis.

clapham-north.notes: 409 Clapham Rd, renovated up-market all-rounder and late-night bar. Multiple screens including plasmas in the back area, full-volume match days, Sunday roast.

falcon-clapham-junction.notes: 2 St John's Hill, Grade II 1887 Nicholson's pub with a 125ft bar counter, once the longest in the country, and a falcon stained-glass window. Sky and TNT, quality pub food, opens 11am.

alexandra-clapham.notes: Two floors with five large HD screens and two projector screens, upstairs darts lounge with four boards, function room, craft beer, cocktails and pizza. Open until 1am Fri and Sat.

food.note: Pizzas between the screens

bread-and-roses.notes: 68 Clapham Manor St, the country's only trade-union-owned pub, run by the Workers Beer Company. Award-winning fringe theatre upstairs, garden room and sheltered rear garden, three microbrewery cask ales, live music every weekend, comedy, open mic, reggae DJs. No sport.

sun-clapham.notes: Clapham Old Town, Mitchells and Butlers. Buzzing beer garden, excellent food menu and good-value roasts, live music and comedy nights. Open until 1am Fri and Sat.

abbeville.notes: Three Cheers Pub Co. Modern British gastropub with free-range meat aged in house, Sunday roasts, dog friendly with biscuits and water bowls.

bedford-balham.notes: Major sporting events screened live; Banana Cabaret and Always Be Comedy nights, regular live music, club nights Fri and Sat; 15 hotel rooms; traditional Sunday roasts.

devonshire-balham.notes: 39 Balham High Rd. Called the best pub garden in Balham; seasonal British food, Sunday roasts (and doggy roasts), Tuesday quiz, private hire, midnight close Fri and Sat. Screens not confirmed in the listing.

selkirk-tooting.notes: 60 Selkirk Rd, Victorian gastropub with vintage furnishings, beer garden, homemade British menu and Sunday roasts; open until midnight Thu-Sat. Screens not confirmed in the listing.

alexandra-wimbledon.notes: 33 Wimbledon Hill Rd. Four bars including a dedicated sports bar with HD TVs and a big screen (Sky Sports), the Loft with an open-air terrace, a fireplace lounge; Burger Shack and Sunday roasts; open until 1am Fri and Sat.

dukes-head-putney.notes: 8 Lower Richmond Rd. Coxswain restaurant with a wall of river windows, Rowing Club room with riverside terrace, three private-hire spaces; screens for tournaments and the Six Nations; seasonal British menu and Sunday roast; midnight close Fri and Sat.

boathouse-putney.notes: 32 Brewhouse Lane, Young's riverside pub with a balcony and ground-floor patio on the Thames, British classics and roasts, two hire spaces for up to 200. Closes 11pm; screens not confirmed in the listing.

antelope-tooting.notes: 76 Mitcham Rd, 1800s pub recently refurbished. Garden and outdoor dining, Sky Sports for the Six Nations and tournaments, gastro menu and Sunday roast, two private-hire rooms, midnight close Fri and Sat.

westow-house.notes: 79 Westow Hill. Two large TV screens for tournaments and the Six Nations, British pub food with a legendary roast, live music, two hire spaces (Waterhouse Bar for 120, the Library). Closes midnight Fri and Sat.

half-moon-herne-hill.notes: 10 Half Moon Lane, Grade II with 12 boutique bedrooms. Gastro menu and breakfasts, Saturday gigs, Wednesday quiz, monthly comedy cabaret, two hire rooms, open until 2am Fri and Sat. Screens not confirmed in the listing.

golden-lion-fulham.notes: 57 Fulham High St, a short walk from Craven Cottage. Multiple screens with Sky and TNT plus outdoor TVs in the beer garden; sourdough pizzas, burgers, tapas and bao buns; open 12 to 11 daily.

food.note: Sourdough pizzas, burgers, tapas and bao buns

defectors-weld.notes: 170 Uxbridge Rd. Screen for the Six Nations rather than a football pub; DJs Friday to Sunday, British pub food and roast, two semi-private hire areas, open until 2am Fri and Sat.

food.note: Pub food, a much-praised burger and a Sunday roast

toucan-soho.notes: 19 Carlisle St. Guinness specialists with a wall of taps and retro posters, Sky Sports popular for Ireland rugby, Celtic dishes on the menu, closes 11pm. Jimi Hendrix played here in the 1960s.

clarence-whitehall.notes: 53 Whitehall. Historic pub, restaurant and event space with private dining rooms; British menu, afternoon tea and roasts; closes 11pm. No sport screens mentioned.

food.note: Pub classics, afternoon tea and Sunday roasts

patch.tip: Quaint Whitehall pub near Downing Street with private dining rooms. Handy for Trafalgar Square, not for the football.

alma-wandsworth.notes: Green-tiled Young's pub opposite Wandsworth Town station with painted mirrors, 23 bedrooms and the Old York function room. Calls itself an iconic sports pub: big screens for the Six Nations, Premier League, Champions League and boxing. Country-style dining room and a famous roast (Top 50 Gastropubs listed).

eight-bells-fulham.notes: 89 Fulham High St, licensed 1629 as the Blue Anchor and the Eight Bells by 1754, the oldest surviving tavern in Fulham. Fulham FC used it as a changing room 1886-88. Five changing ales plus St Peter's Organic Best, home-cooked food and well-reviewed roasts. Reserved for AWAY fans on Fulham match days.

food.note: Home-cooked food with a well-reviewed Sunday roast

patch.tip: The oldest pub in Fulham, licensed in 1629, where Fulham FC once changed before matches. Five cask ales and a proper roast. Note: away fans only on match days.

durell-arms.notes: 704 Fulham Rd. Six HD screens and two large projectors with Sky, TNT and terrestrial sport; booths with their own screens. Quiz Tuesdays 8pm, live music some nights, garden, child and dog friendly.

patch.tip: Eight screens including two projectors, and booths with a screen of their own. Quiz on Tuesdays, garden out back.

white-horse-parsons-green.notes: The Sloaney Pony. Coaching inn on the site since at least 1688, mentioned in The Spectator in 1712. Renowned beer list, terrace overlooking Parsons Green packed on sunny days, quizzes, DJ sets and live sport screenings. Fully refurbished recently.

duke-on-the-green.notes: 235 New Kings Rd overlooking Parsons Green. Seasonal British pub food, roast with double-egg Yorkshires, cocktails, outdoor seating on the green, very dog friendly. No live sport advertised.

patch.tip: Handsome pub looking straight onto Parsons Green, with tables out front and a roast worth the walk. Dogs get treats, nobody gets a screen.

broadway-bar-fulham.notes: Official Chelsea FC fans pub on Fulham Rd, reopened December 2024 with five big screens and game-day burger menus; a rooftop and live music are also listed. CAMRA's entry still carries a 'closed, future uncertain' flag, so check before travelling.

patch.tip: The official Chelsea fans' pub on the Broadway, reopened in December 2024 with big screens and game-day burgers. Worth ringing ahead: its status has wobbled.

rutland-arms.notes: 15 Lower Mall by Hammersmith Bridge, opened c.1849 and rebuilt in the 1870s; lost its top floor in the Blitz. Greene King Abbot and IPA, lounge bar with rowing sculls on the ceiling, rear dining area, first-floor balcony bar for functions, bench seats at the front facing the river. Midnight Fri and Sat. No sport advertised.

patch.tip: Riverside pub by Hammersmith Bridge with sculls hanging from the ceiling and benches out front facing the water. A balcony bar upstairs for parties.

old-ship-hammersmith.notes: 25 Upper Mall, serving the riverside since 1722. Enormous two-tier terrace over the Thames plus a veranda and railed patio; first-floor balcony is a Boat Race spot. Sport on the screens inside. Renovated 2018 and 2024.

patch.tip: Two tiers of terrace over the Thames and one of the best Boat Race balconies in London. Screens inside for everything else.

lamb-chiswick.notes: 9 Barley Mow Passage, on the site of the Battle of Turnham Green. Traditional interiors, exposed brick, open fire, beer garden, real ale, traditional Sunday roast, board games, BBQ, bookable space, dog and child friendly. No live sport advertised.

food.note: Classic British menu with a traditional Sunday roast, and a BBQ in the garden in summer

patch.tip: Tucked off the High Road on the site of the Battle of Turnham Green: open fire, board games and a garden for the summer BBQ.

sindercombe-social.notes: 2 Goldhawk Rd on the corner of Shepherds Bush Green, renamed 2014. Large screens throughout plus a projector and commentary for major events. Live music Monday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday; cocktails, craft beer, sourdough pizza and burgers.

food.note: Sourdough pizzas, burgers and pub favourites, plus sandwiches in the afternoon

patch.tip: Big screens the length of the room plus a projector with commentary, then a band four nights a week.

queen-adelaide-bush.notes: Closed end of June 2025; the Grade II building is being reopened as the Talli Queen, an Indian pub and dining room, so its QPR match-day role is gone. Removed.

brewery-tap-brentford.notes: 47 Catherine Wheel Rd. Family-run riverside pub with a sunny beer garden, Santa Maria pizza, live music five nights a week with free entry and a resident pianist, Monday quiz, pool table, Saturday BBQ and Sunday roast. Dog friendly.

food.note: Santa Maria pizza, a Saturday BBQ in the garden and a Sunday roast

patch.tip: Family-run riverside pub with pizza, a garden and free live music five nights a week. The Bees drink here, but it's a music pub first.

magpie-and-crown.notes: 128 High St, original pub 1614, rebuilt in the 1920s-30s as mock Tudor. On CAMRA's local inventory; reckons 2,163 different real ales sold since 1996, six on at a time. Lanna Thai Kitchen seven days, pool table, front tables, rear covered patio, live music three or four nights a week.

food.note: Lanna Thai Kitchen, open seven days

patch.tip: Mock-Tudor free house that has poured over two thousand different cask ales since 1996, with a Thai kitchen and live music most weeks.

express-tavern.notes: 56 Kew Bridge Rd, a landmark for 200 years, building from the 1860s, an old London-to-Bath coaching stop. Now run by Big Smoke Brew Co: ten ale handpumps in the small bar and up to five ciders in the saloon, largely original interior, spacious beer garden. Minutes from the Gtech.

patch.tip: Ten handpumps and five ciders in a largely untouched Victorian interior, with a big garden. The civilised stop before the Gtech.

one-over-the-ait.notes: Fuller's pub on the Thames by Kew Bridge. Numerous screens showing up to three games at once, TNT Sports, and a Players' Lounge upstairs with interactive games, a private bar and more screens. Minutes from the Gtech.

patch.tip: Fuller's riverside pub by Kew Bridge that shows three games at once, with a Players' Lounge upstairs. Walking distance from the Gtech.

black-dog-brentford.notes: 17 Albany Rd, building from at least 1861 rebuilt 1901, reopened October 2018 as a free house after a rough history. Fourteen craft keg lines, four cask ales from independents and three ciders, natural and organic wines, log fires, beer garden, vegan Sunday roasts. Closed Tuesdays.

food.note: Pub kitchen with a Sunday roast, vegan roast included

patch.tip: Backstreet beer house with fourteen keg lines, four casks and log fires. Closed Tuesdays, so check before you walk over.

north-star-ealing.notes: 43 The Broadway, built early 1800s and locally listed for its unusual design; three rooms each divided by a fireplace, refurbished 2014. Fuller's London Pride, garden patio alongside the pub, partially covered and heated. Child and dog friendly.

patch.tip: Early-1800s pub on the Broadway with three fire-divided rooms and a heated side garden. Pride on the pumps.

grove-ealing.notes: Opposite Ealing Green and the old Ealing Studios. Six screens with Sky, TNT and terrestrial and two Sky boxes so different games run at once. Large heated wraparound front and side garden with covered seating looking onto the green and Pitzhanger Manor. Real ale; was in the Michelin Guide 2015.

patch.tip: Six screens and two Sky boxes, so several games at once, and a big heated garden facing Ealing Green.

drayton-court.notes: Neo-gothic Fuller's pub-hotel opened 1894 with one of London's largest beer gardens, extended in 2016 with a summer bar. Fringe theatre inside and Shakespeare in the Garden productions. Award-winning handmade pies and Fuller's cask ales.

food.note: Award-winning handmade pies and a Sunday roast

patch.tip: Neo-gothic Fuller's hotel-pub from 1894 with one of the largest beer gardens in London, a fringe theatre inside and Shakespeare out in the garden in summer.

elgin-ladbroke-grove.notes: 96 Ladbroke Grove, Grade II with what CAMRA calls the crown jewel of Victorian glazed screens. Five or more TV screens for the Premier League, FA Cup, Champions League, Europa League and Six Nations. Weekly quiz, private rooms, dogs welcome throughout.

patch.tip: Grade II gin palace with the most spectacular Victorian glazed screens in London, and five modern ones showing the football.

metropolitan-w2.notes: 60 Great Western Rd, right beside Westbourne Park station. Victorian pub with a large beer garden and roof terrace, pool table, jukebox, craft beer list, weekly comedy and acoustic nights and a Sunday movie matinee. No live sport advertised.

patch.tip: Victorian corner pub by the station with a big garden, a roof terrace, a jukebox and a Sunday movie matinee. Portobello is minutes away.

sports-bar-marylebone.notes: At Marylebone station with entrances from the concourse and the street. Twenty 52-inch HD screens with full Sky and TNT coverage of football, rugby, tennis, snooker and NFL. New booths; private Scarlet Bar for 50 and a basement restaurant and bar for 150.

patch.tip: Twenty HD screens either side of the Marylebone concourse, with booths and a basement room for big groups.

porterhouse-covent-garden.notes: 21-22 Maiden Lane, open since 2000, one of central London's largest bars over three floors with three bars. Porters, stouts and ales brewed at its own Dublin brewery. Eighteen screens; thinks of itself as a rugby pub. Live music in the basement Thursday to Saturday, large terrace.

patch.tip: Three floors, eighteen screens and beer brewed at its own Dublin brewery. A rugby pub at heart, with one of the West End's biggest terraces.

de-hems.notes: Macclesfield St off Shaftesbury Ave. Dutch cafe bar since 1959, named for a retired Dutch seaman who ran it as an oyster bar; a Dutch resistance meeting point in the war. Six HD screens plus one huge screen in the upstairs bar, Sky and TNT, specialising in Eredivisie, Premier League, Champions League and internationals. Dutch and Belgian beers.

patch.tip: London's Dutch pub since 1959, and a resistance meeting point before that. Seven screens including a big one upstairs, Eredivisie included.

waxy-oconnors.notes: 14-16 Rupert St. Four bars over six levels linked by staircases and passages. Nine screens including three large projector screens, with fanzone areas for GAA, rugby, football, racing, tennis and golf. Live music seven nights a week, Irish trad on Sundays. Over-18s only.

patch.tip: Four bars over six levels, nine screens including three projectors, and a fanzone for everything from GAA to golf. Live music every night.

oneills-wardour.notes: 33-37 Wardour St, three floors, 900 capacity, on the old site of the Flamingo Jazz Club and the WAG Club. Ten HD TVs and two projector screens, hireable areas with their own screens, booths with a screen each. Live music every night, DJs.

patch.tip: Three floors on the site of the old Flamingo Jazz Club: ten HD screens, two projectors, booths with their own telly, and a band every night.

counting-house.notes: Grade II Victorian banking hall built 1893 as Prescott's Bank, Fuller's since 1997; domed skylight over the old counting chamber. Award-winning handmade pies, fish and chips, Sunday roast, and 15 boutique hotel rooms above. No live sport advertised.

food.note: Award-winning handmade pies, fish and chips and a Sunday roast under the dome

patch.tip: Fuller's in an 1893 banking hall, with a domed skylight over the old counting chamber and a pie menu worth the trip. Hotel rooms upstairs.

sports-bar-farringdon.notes: 19-25 Cowcross St, trading as The Boundary. Twenty 52 and 60 inch plasma screens plus a video screen wall, live sport and news feeds, booths upstairs and along the room.

patch.name: The Boundary (Sports Bar & Grill)
patch.tip: Twenty plasmas and a video screen wall a minute from Farringdon station, with booths if you want to claim a corner.

wellington-waterloo.notes: Nicholson's pub round the corner from Waterloo, with Sky Sports and TNT on several screens.

hole-in-the-wall.notes: Inside a railway arch opposite Waterloo's Victory Arch; trains rumble overhead. Six cask ales and 25+ taps, four handpumps in the front bar and six in the back, mostly London and southern independents. Unchanged dive-bar decor, folk music on Sunday evenings. Cited in the 1975 CAMRA Good Beer Guide.

patch.tip: Literally inside a railway arch opposite Waterloo, with trains overhead, six casks and twenty-five taps. Folk music on Sunday nights.

hanover-arms.notes: 326 Kennington Park Rd, 100m from Oval station. Narrow Victorian interior with moulded cornice, ceiling roses and shamrock bunting; resolutely Irish, mixed-age crowd. Two big screens with all live Sky Sports, pavement seating.

patch.tip: Narrow Irish local a hundred metres from Oval station, shamrock bunting and all. Two big screens with Sky on for everything.

east-dulwich-tavern.notes: 1 Lordship Lane on the corner of Goose Green, open since 1999, reopened after a 1m refurbishment. Screens for the big games with Sky and TNT, plus an upstairs space for tournament viewing. Weekly quiz and a packed events calendar.

patch.tip: Corner pub on Goose Green with Sky and TNT downstairs and an upstairs room that fills for tournaments. Weekly quiz.

bishop-east-dulwich.notes: 25 Lordship Lane, formerly the Foresters Arms. Seasonal British pub food, local and British cask plus continental beers, cosy corners and a spacious outdoor area, live music Fridays 7-10, open until 2am Friday and Saturday. No sport advertised.

food.note: Seasonal British home-cooked pub food and a Sunday roast

patch.tip: Lordship Lane local with seasonal cooking, a big outdoor area and live music on Fridays. Open till 2am at weekends, and no screens.

actress-dulwich.notes: 90 Crystal Palace Rd, just off Lordship Lane. Wood Stone oven pizzas, pub classics and Sunday roasts; big screens for live sport, sun-trap garden, quiz nights, family friendly. Voted best pub in Dulwich by Time Out and the Londonist.

food.note: Stone-baked pizzas from a Wood Stone oven, pub classics and a Sunday roast

patch.tip: Wood-fired pizzas, a sun-trap garden and big screens for the football. Voted best pub in Dulwich by Time Out.

blythe-hill-tavern.notes: Victorian corner pub, Grade II listed in 2022 for a nationally important three-room interior with 1920s panelling. Three regular and one changing beer, celebrated cider list (CAMRA National Cider Pub finalist 2018, branch Pub of the Year 2015 and 2018). Traditional Irish music Tuesdays, live sport, poetry nights, Van Dough pizzas.

food.note: Van Dough pizzas in the bar

patch.tip: Grade II Victorian three-room local with a nationally important interior, a famous cider list and Irish music on Tuesdays.

white-hart-crystal-palace.notes: 96 Church Rd at the southern apex of the Triangle, back to its original name after a spell as an imitation Irish bar. 250k refurbishment gave the garden four heated ski-lodge huts, new lighting and a mural. Three handpumps (Doom Bar, Tribute), open kitchen, open mic Thursdays, DJs Friday and Saturday, quiz Mondays.

food.note: Traditional pub food from an open kitchen, plus a Sunday roast

patch.tip: Garden full of heated ski-lodge huts at the southern tip of the Triangle. Open mic Thursdays, DJs at weekends.

railway-telegraph.notes: 19 Brigstock Rd, built 1876, Young's freehold from 1901, now Ram Pub Company. Two distinct bars, patio garden and smoking area, two regular cask ales, evening meals. Shows all major sport and explicitly welcomes football supporters heading to Selhurst Park.

food.note: Evening meals from the pub kitchen

patch.tip: 1876 pub near Thornton Heath station with a patio garden, real ale and a welcome for both sets of fans walking up to Selhurst.

dolphin-sydenham.notes: 121 Sydenham Rd, a pub on the site for 200 years, rebuilt by Courage in the 1930s in Brewers' Tudor. Large landscaped garden with fountains, sculpture and gravel paths. Four cask ales plus craft keg, wood-fired pizzas and some of the best Sunday roasts in south London. No sport found.

food.note: Wood-fired pizzas, pub classics and a Sunday roast with a reputation across south London

patch.tip: Brewers' Tudor pub with a landscaped garden of fountains and sculpture, wood-fired pizza and one of the best roasts in south London.

commercial-herne-hill.notes: 210-212 Railton Rd. On CAMRA's regional inventory as one of 133 London pubs with an interior of special historic interest: 1930s counters, bar-back, fireplaces and fielded panelling. Live Sky and TNT, order-at-table service on match days, roaring open fire, beer garden, close to Brockwell Park.

patch.tip: A 1930s interior on CAMRA's historic register, an open fire, a garden, and Sky and TNT with order-at-table on match days.

northcote-battersea.notes: Corner of Battersea Rise and Northcote Rd, five minutes from Clapham Junction. Young's-managed since 2023, Geronimo before that. Six screens with Sky and TNT for the Premier League, Champions League, Six Nations and finals; bookable tables in the main bar and the Common Room.

patch.tip: Six screens with Sky and TNT five minutes from Clapham Junction, and you can book a table in the Common Room for the big ones.

eagle-ale-house.notes: 104 Chatham Rd, just off Northcote Rd. Many-time CAMRA award winner: micro-brewery cask and keykeg, a handpump kept for cider, Lambics in the coolers. Leather sofas, old bottles and books; large beer garden with a heated shelter and marquee. Several screens come alive for major events, mainly rugby. Opens 3pm on weekdays.

patch.tip: CAMRA-garlanded ale house off Northcote Road with sofas, Lambics and a heated marquee in the garden. Screens wake up for the rugby.

sultan-colliers-wood.notes: 78 Norman Rd, the only Hop Back Brewery pub in London, rescued from closure by Hop Back in 1994. 1930s roadhouse with a regionally important historic interior on CAMRA's inventory; two drinking areas, outside seating, about six handpumps plus keg and bottles. Darts, board and card games, open mic, acoustic and English folk sessions, cabaret. Ten minutes from Colliers Wood and South Wimbledon.

patch.tip: London's only Hop Back pub, a 1930s roadhouse with a listed-quality interior, saved by the brewery in 1994. Folk sessions and darts, not a screen pub.

drayton-park-arms.notes: 66 Drayton Park N5 1ND, opposite the stadium approach and by Drayton Park station; Arsenal tube is the nearest walk past the club shop. Fully renovated and reopened in 2024 with stained glass and solid wood. Quizzes and music nights. Open 2pm weekdays, noon at weekends.

patch.tip: Renovated in 2024 and a short walk from the Emirates past the club shop. Arsenal to the core on match days, quizzes and music the rest of the week.

duke-of-wellington-haggerston.notes: 260 Haggerston Rd, an attractive three-storey Italianate pub looking over Stonebridge Common, named when Wellington became Prime Minister. Has a big screen for football, a pool table and a dartboard, plus a smoking area. Opens 4pm on weekdays, 2pm Fri and Sat.

patch.tip: Handsome three-storey Italianate pub looking over Stonebridge Common, named when Wellington took office. Pool, darts and a big screen for the football.

bull-highgate.notes: North Hill (not North Road), Grade II. Brewpub with the London Brewing Company kit in the rear garden. Seasonal British food and Sunday roasts, dining area and garden, disabled access. Acquired by Metropolitan Pub Co (Greene King) in March 2022.

patch.tip: Highgate brewpub with the London Brewing Company kit out in the garden, and a seasonal kitchen to go with it.

pig-and-butcher.notes: 80 Liverpool Rd, opened 2012 in a mid-1800s building on the old livestock route to Smithfield. Whole animals butchered on site in a basement butchery; native and rare-breed meat direct from farmers, daily-changing menu. Michelin Guide and Top 50 Gastropubs listed.

island-queen.notes: 87 Noel Rd, Grade II, built 1851 and altered 1889 and 1897. A three-star pub on CAMRA's National Inventory: an interior of outstanding national importance with etched and cut glass by R Morris & Son, glazed screenwork, a high Lincrusta ceiling and mosaic entrance floors. Near the canal.

patch.tip: An 1851 gin palace by the canal with glazed screens, cut glass and a Lincrusta ceiling. One of only a handful of London interiors CAMRA rates nationally outstanding.

earl-of-essex.notes: 25 Danbury St, a former Watney pub reopened as a beer house in 2012. Nearly 20 taps and pumps including up to 14 keg lines, some from the owners' Saint Monday brewery, plus cans and bottles. Small beer garden at the back and a seasonal menu of pub classics.

lansdowne.notes: 90 Gloucester Ave, in Primrose Hill since 1992. Mediterranean and British cooking, hand-stretched thin-crust pizzas often called among London's best, Sunday roast. Private dining plus the Vinyl Room, a private karaoke space.

patch.food.note: Hand-stretched thin-crust pizzas, Mediterranean plates and a Sunday roast, in the bar or the dining room

hawley-arms.notes: 2 Castlehaven Rd. Fairy lights, leather booths and a walled garden downstairs; first-floor bar with a roof terrace, log fires and a jukebox. Amy Winehouse's local until 2011, along with Noel Fielding, Pete Doherty and Kate Moss; a mural of her covers the back wall.

patch.tip: Amy Winehouse's local: fairy lights and booths downstairs, a roof terrace and log fires up top, and a mural of her across the back wall.

lock-tavern.notes: 35 Chalk Farm Rd opposite Camden Market, a McMullen's pub since 2024. Two floors with a rear ground-floor patio and a roof terrace over Camden Market; resident DJs Friday and Saturday in the cocktail lounge, live music weekly, Sunday roast.

patch.food.note: Pub kitchen and a Sunday roast

dublin-castle.notes: 94 Parkway. Built for Irish navvies, made its name in the late 1970s when Madness built a following here; hosted Coldplay's first gig under that name in 1998 and was one of Amy Winehouse's haunts. Pub at the front, 200-capacity music room at the back with a door charge in the evening.

patch.tip: Madness made their name here and Coldplay played their first gig under that name in 1998. Pub at the front, 200-capacity gig room at the back.

tapping-the-admiral.notes: 77 Castle Rd near Kentish Town West. Eight changing cask beers with a promise of at least two brewed within 30 miles. Four-time CAMRA North London Pub of the Year (2013, 2015, 2018, 2023). Reopened 2011 after four years derelict; named for the sailors who drank the brandy preserving Nelson's body.

patch.tip: Eight changing casks and four CAMRA Pub of the Year titles. Named for the sailors who tapped the brandy barrel carrying Nelson home.

high-cross.notes: 350 High Rd, a converted 1920s toilet block at the Monument Way junction, with the lit ladies' and gents' signs and original tiling kept. Ten rotating keg lines of craft beer plus local Bohem and Redemption, cocktails and a short menu.

food.note: A short menu of classics alongside the beer

patch.tip: A 1920s public convenience turned beer bar, original tiling and all, with ten rotating keg lines.

hand-in-hand-wimbledon.notes: 6 Crooked Billet on the edge of the Common, dating to 1831 and originally a bakery, with the oven nook still there to sit in. A family beer house for 100 years before Young's bought it in 1974; sold on in 2006. Good Beer Guide regular for over two decades, CAMRA SW London Pub of the Year 2013. Young's Bitter plus Hogsback, Adnams and Wimbledon Brewery. Dog friendly with free biscuits and a Dog of the Day award.

patch.tip: An 1831 bakery turned ale house on the edge of the Common: sit in the old oven nook, and the dogs get biscuits and a Dog of the Day prize.

crooked-billet-wimbledon.notes: 14-15 Crooked Billet facing the Common. Building from the early 18th century, the Crooked Billet from the 1750s; Young's leased it in 1888 and bought the freehold in 1928. Wood-panelled interior, restaurant and garden, Young's London Original plus a changing beer, British pub food.

cats-back.notes: 86-88 Point Pleasant, Wandsworth, bought by Harvey's in 2012. Small Victorian pub with a bohemian front bar, upstairs function room, decked beer garden, five minutes from the Thames. Full range of Harvey's plus guests, cocktails, music, film and art nights. Joint first in CAMRA's Joe Goodwin award for best corner street local.

patch.tip: Small Victorian corner local bought by Harvey's, with the full range on, a decked garden and film and art nights upstairs.

spencer-putney.notes: 237 Lower Richmond Rd, back to the name Spencer Arms after Market Taverns took over in summer 2023. Victorian tavern overlooking Putney Lower Common: large sunlit dining room, fireside area with leather banquettes, dog-friendly patio, and licensed seating out on the common in summer.

patch.name: The Spencer Arms
patch.tip: Victorian tavern facing Putney Lower Common, with a sunlit dining room, a fireside lounge and tables out on the grass in summer.

bricklayers-arms-putney.notes: 32 Waterman St, built 1826 on a coaching house and forge site as the Waterman's Arms, renamed late 19th century. Family-owned free house reopened 2005; for a time the only London pub serving the full Timothy Taylor range, with Boltmaker and Landlord regular plus local guests. CAMRA Greater London Pub of the Year 2007 and 2009, SW London 2006, 2008 and 2010.

patch.tip: An 1826 free house that was once the only pub in London pouring the full Timothy Taylor range. Twice CAMRA's Greater London Pub of the Year.

woodman-battersea.notes: 60 Battersea High St behind Battersea Square. Hall & Woodhouse pub with three regular ales; quirky courtyard garden with oak barrel tables, stacked logs, candlelit corners and a pizza oven. Country-style interior, substantial food trade, family friendly.

food.note: Hearty British cooking plus pizzas from the oven in the courtyard garden

patch.tip: Hidden behind Battersea Square: a candlelit courtyard of barrel tables and stacked logs, with a pizza oven in the corner.

prince-albert-battersea.notes: 85 Albert Bridge Rd, serving since 1866, opposite the Albert Gate into Battersea Park. Victorian corner pub with an impressive island bar, popular summer garden, real ale, British classics and Sunday roasts, dog and family friendly. Bridge Room for private hire plus semi-private Hunter's Corner and Royal Garden.

patch.tip: Victorian corner pub facing the Albert Gate into Battersea Park, with an island bar and a garden that fills the moment the sun comes out.

florence-herne-hill.notes: Opposite Brockwell Park near Herne Hill station. One of the first modern brewpubs in 2007, but the Florence Brewery kit was removed in a spring 2023 refurbishment to expand the dining room. Central island bar, rear dining room open to the kitchen, garden and a well-equipped children's playroom; modern British food, one regular and one changing beer.

patch.food.note: Modern British cooking from an open kitchen, with a Sunday lunch built for groups
patch.tip: Opposite Brockwell Park, with a garden and a proper children's playroom. It brewed its own until 2023; now the kitchen is the draw.

crown-and-greyhound.notes: 73 Dulwich Village, Grade II, known locally as the Dog. Built as a pub-hotel around 1900 from two premises, one for gentry and one for labourers; internal screens, etched glazing and a fine bar-back. Large paved front area and landscaped rear garden, 20 boutique bedrooms some with 1900s fireplaces. Reopened 2017 and refreshed March 2026. Two to four changing real ales.

patch.tip: Known as the Dog: a 1900 pub-hotel built as two pubs in one, with etched glass, a landscaped garden and twenty rooms upstairs.

palmerston.notes: 91 Lordship Lane, built in the 1860s with two rooms and Victorian fittings including the bar-back and mosaic floor; the Lord Palmerston bar signage was added in the 1960s. Refurbished and reopened early 2026. Premium but relaxed gastropub with a long international wine list.

sylvan-post.notes: 24-28 Dartmouth Rd in a former 1960s post office; ex-Antic, taken over by Portobello Brewery in late 2020. Two original safe vaults with full-height doors converted into snugs, the strong room another, walls of postal memorabilia and old post office equipment. Good food with Sunday lunch a speciality.

patch.tip: A 1960s post office turned pub, where the old safe vaults are now snugs you can sit inside and the walls are hung with telegrams.

dartmouth-arms.notes: Closed 30 March 2026 when MEATliquor shut a number of venues; long-term closed, future uncertain. Removed.

sparrowhawk.notes: 2 Westow Hill on the corner of Westow Street at the top of the Triangle, under new ownership since summer 2024. Modern open layout with a long bar, beer garden, live music and a room for hire. Nine TVs showing live sport. Brunch, sharing plates, proper Sunday roasts and a serious wine list.

patch.tip: Nine screens at the top of the Triangle, a garden out back and a wine list that takes itself seriously.

oval-tavern.notes: 131 Oval Rd, down a residential street near East Croydon. Six handpumps with up to four cask ales, in every Good Beer Guide since 2015. Live music mainly jazz, blues and folk, plus sessions, klezmer and morris dancing; garden on the lower level with hops and barbecue grills.

patch.tip: Croydon's music pub: jazz, blues and folk most weeks, six handpumps, and a garden with hops growing up it.

dog-and-bull-croydon.notes: 24-25 Surrey St, Grade II 18th-century building with a 19th-century frontage on the site of a 12th or 13th century inn, the Bell; understood to be Croydon's oldest pub. Young's from the 1830s until 2025, now a Laine pub under Punch and rebranded The Dog. The old yard, once an animal pound on Butcher's Row, is the beer garden.

patch.name: The Dog (ex Dog & Bull)
patch.tip: Croydon's oldest pub, Grade II and on the site of a medieval inn. Young's for nearly two centuries until 2025, now rebranded The Dog.

catford-bridge-tavern.notes: Mock Tudor pub saved from closure by a local campaign in 2012 and CAMRA South East London Pub of the Year 2013 under Antic. Gutted by fire in March 2016 (eight engines, 58 firefighters), reopened end of March 2017. Acquired by Portobello Brewery in June 2023, which reinstalled three handpumps.

patch.tip: Saved by its neighbours, then gutted by fire in 2016 and rebuilt. Portobello took it on in 2023 and put the handpumps back.

fox-and-firkin.notes: 316 Lewisham High St. Live music or DJs almost every night: jazz jams, folk, reggae, indie, punk, sound system parties. Sprawling garden, said to be south London's biggest pub garden, with a Backstage Bar and a 1950s train carriage for bookings. Own Firkin Brewery house beers; pizzas, toasties and a Sunday dinner menu.

food.note: Pizzas and toasties in the evenings plus a Sunday dinner menu

patch.tip: Live music or DJs almost every night and a garden with its own bar and a 1950s train carriage in it. They brew their own too.

kings-arms-roupell.notes: 25 Roupell St, Grade II early-to-mid 19th century, halfway down a period backstreet used constantly as a film location. Nine real ale pumps with a constantly changing list. Kanchana's Kitchen serves Thai seven days a week, run as a separate business. No reservations for either.

patch.tip: Nine handpumps in a Grade II pub on the prettiest backstreet in Waterloo, with Kanchana's Thai kitchen in the conservatory. No bookings.

anchor-and-hope-waterloo.notes: 36 The Cut, by the Old and Young Vic. Pioneering gastropub: modern European, menu changes with the season, no reservations and shared tables. The Sunday lunch, slow-roast shoulder, whole partridges and bowl-sized Yorkshires, is the most recommended roast south of the river. Pre-theatre sitting.

patch.tip: The pioneering gastropub on The Cut: no bookings, shared tables, and a Sunday roast that people cross the river for.

prince-of-wales-cleaver.notes: 48 Cleaver Square, an independent pub on a preserved Georgian square with a tree-lined boules and petanque pitch. Drinks served in plastic to take onto the square and they lend you a boules set. Food Wednesday to Sunday including a well-regarded roast. Once a Richardson gang haunt.

patch.tip: They will lend you a boules set and serve your pint in a plastic so you can play on the Georgian square outside. Roast on Sundays.

fentiman-arms.notes: Quiet residential street between Oval, Vauxhall and Kennington, close enough to the Oval to hear the cricket. Geronimo Inns design; handsome garden lit with festoon lights, private room upstairs, real fire, dog friendly, quality British food.

royal-vauxhall-tavern.notes: Built 1860-62 on land that was part of the Vauxhall Pleasure Gardens. Listed Grade II on 8 September 2015, the first building in the UK listed in recognition of its importance to LGBTQ history. A drag and cabaret venue since the later 19th century and known for ground-breaking alternative cabaret.

patch.tip: Built on the old Vauxhall Pleasure Gardens and the first building in Britain listed for its LGBTQ+ history. Cabaret here since the 1800s.

windmill-brixton.notes: 22 Blenheim Gardens, capacity 150, ten minutes from Brixton tube. Opened 1971 as a local, became an Irish music hub under Seamus McCausland from 1992, then a cutting-edge booking policy from 2002 under Tim Perry. Emerging indie, alternative and experimental acts seven nights a week; surprise shows from Calexico, Stereolab and Scritti Politti. Entry usually 4 to 5 pounds. Third best music venue in London in a Time Out poll.

patch.tip: A 150-capacity room that punches far above it: seven nights of new bands, surprise shows and entry for a fiver.

harwood-arms.notes: London's only Michelin-starred pub, holding the star since soon after it opened in 2009. Game and wild food led, with specialist venison, Jersey beef and Iberian pork; the venison Scotch egg is the dish that made Scotch eggs fashionable again. Head chef Josh Cutress; Brett Graham of the three-star Ledbury a director since 2009.

patch.tip: London's only Michelin-starred pub, and the place that made the Scotch egg fashionable again with its venison one. Book weeks out.

fox-and-pheasant.notes: 1 Billing Rd, built c.1846-8 as the Bedford Arms, then the Prince of Wales, renamed the Fox & Pheasant in 1965. Sold by Greene King in 2017 to James Blunt and his wife Sofia, restored and reopened 27 June 2018. On CAMRA's National Inventory of Historic Pub Interiors; cosy bar and a conservatory, near Stamford Bridge. Top 50 Gastropubs.

phene-chelsea.notes: 9 Phene St, pronounced Feeny, built 1853 by Dr John Samuel Phene, the man credited with the idea of planting street trees. Saloon bar with red banquettes, conservatory restaurant and a first-floor lounge; extensive heated side terrace with sofas, outdoor fireplaces and hanging basket chairs. A Made in Chelsea fixture.

patch.tip: A heated terrace of sofas, outdoor fireplaces and hanging chairs, built in 1853 by the man who invented the street tree.

cross-keys-chelsea.notes: 1 Lawrence St, built 1708 and the oldest pub in Chelsea; its name has never changed. Regulars have included Turner, Whistler and Sargent, Agatha Christie and Dylan Thomas, Bob Marley and the Rolling Stones. Closed in 2012 for a mansion conversion, saved by a local campaign in 2013 and reopened. Now run by Butcombe.

patch.tip: Chelsea's oldest pub, built in 1708 and never renamed. Turner, Whistler, Dylan Thomas and Bob Marley all drank here; locals saved it from becoming a house in 2013.

surprise-chelsea.notes: 6 Christchurch Terrace, a local landmark since 1853, named after HMS Surprise, a captured French warship. Relaunched under hotelier Jack Greenall: bar plus a 28-cover restaurant and the Hamilton private dining room. British-inspired cooking, under ten minutes from Sloane Square.

blue-anchor-hammersmith.notes: 13 Lower Mall, first licensed 9 June 1722 to John Savery as the Blew Anchor and Washhouses; Grade II, present building around the 1890s. A whole sheep was roasted outside in January 1789. Sombre collection of First World War artefacts. Riverside benches on the Mall.

black-lion-hammersmith.notes: 2 South Black Lion Lane, Grade II, close to the river. Beer garden seating 200 around a 400-year-old chestnut tree with Sunday lunchtime barbecues and a vintage skittle alley. Three cask pumps, pub classics, kids' menu and pizzas Friday and Saturday. A painting of A P Herbert presides over his corner table. A Boat Race spot.

food.note: Pub classics and a Sunday roast, pizzas on Friday and Saturday, barbecues in the garden on Sunday lunchtimes

patch.tip: A garden for 200 under a 400-year-old chestnut tree, with a vintage skittle alley and A P Herbert watching from his corner.

andover-arms.notes: 57 Aldensley Rd, an 1853 backstreet local at the centre of Brackenbury Village, bought by Fuller's from Watney's in 1991. Wood-panelled bar with an elaborate back bar, eclectic seating with dining tables, open-plan kitchen, piano and fireplace. Frequent Good Beer Guide entry; strong reputation for food and Sunday roasts.

bell-and-crown.notes: Strand on the Green, first licensed as the Bell in 1751, bought by Fuller's in 1814 and rebuilt 1907; conservatory extension 1984. Rear patio and conservatory over the Thames, open river terrace that catches the sun, real log fire opposite the bar. London Pride plus a changing cask, refined pub classics and famous Sunday roasts. Refreshed January 2026.

city-barge.notes: 27 Strand-on-the-Green, built 1484 as the Navigators Arms and renamed in the 19th century when the Lord Mayor moored his barge outside. The Beatles were filmed being chased into it by bagpipers for Help! on 24 April 1965, though the interiors were shot at Twickenham. Extensively refurbished in 2014.

patch.tip: Built in 1484 and renamed when the Lord Mayor moored his barge outside. The Beatles were chased into it by bagpipers in Help!

tabard-chiswick.notes: Bath Rd by Turnham Green, designed by Norman Shaw in 1880 for the Bedford Park garden suburb. Grade II*, with tiling by William de Morgan and Walter Crane and Arts and Crafts mirrors. The 88-seat Tabard Theatre sits above the pub, licensed since 1985; briefly the Chiswick Playhouse from 2019, closed March 2022, back as the Tabard in September 2022. Original William Morris tiles were found behind the theatre wallpaper.

patch.tip: Norman Shaw designed it in 1880 for Bedford Park, with de Morgan and Walter Crane tiles and an 88-seat theatre above the bar.

princess-victoria.notes: Uxbridge Rd, dating from 1829 and one of London's earliest gin palaces, once a tram-commuter stop for a quick gin and water. Briefly Richard Branson's music venue in the 1980s, where Phil Collins filmed Sussudio and One More Night.
